title: Route chat commands through a table filed by hash code

blocks.text: The team's chat-ops bot reads a command from each message and runs it. Its `CommandTable` turns the typed name into the command's position, which `reply` switches on. The table files commands by `hashCode()` when it is built, and the admin page that lists those groups has to keep working, so `byHash` stays.

items: `file(command)`: put a command into `byHash` while the table is built;
`indexOf(name)`: the typed name's position in the command list, or `-1` when it is no command.

blocks.text: When you're done, every command the table was built with is found at its own position, any other name is unknown, and a message with no command text (`indexOf(null)`) is unknown too, not an error. About twelve lines in total.
The tests build their tables from their own command names, and type each name as a new `String`.

cases.says: each command is found at its position and a name that is no command gives -1
commands whose hash codes are equal are each found at their own position
a name whose hash code equals one command's, but which is not that command, gives -1
a null name gives -1 instead of an exception

origin.section: A switch on Strings Is a hashCode lookupswitch Followed by equals

concepts: A switch on a String switches on hashCode() and then compares every label with that hash using equals, so colliding strings reach their own case and a string that only shares a hash falls to default.
A null selector makes a String switch without case null throw NullPointerException from its hashCode() call.
